newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - First Boston starts lodging firms.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - First Boston starts lodging firms.

text.p: First Boston said it initiated coverage of several lodging companies.
-- said started Bristol Hotel Co, Doubletree Corp, Host Marriott Corp as a strong buy.
-- said started La Quinta Inns Inc, ITT Corp, and Marriott International Inc as a buy.
-- said starts Promus Hotel Corp as a hold.
-- said lodging industry fundamentals remain strong, with occupany holding steady and room rates rising at a pace that is ahead of inflation.
-- said demand for hotel rooms is projected to grow at an annual rate of 2.2 percent through 1999.
-- set a 12-18 month price target of $70 a share for Marriott. Said earnings per share are expected to grow 15 percent this year and accelerate to almost 20 percent in 1998.
-- set a 12-18 month price target in the mid-$20s for La Quinta. Said La Quinta has just completed a four-year transformation and moved into an aggressive expansion mode.

-- said Doubletree's concentration in the upscale, full-service segment should continue to produce attractive same-store sales gains. Said Doubletree should see annual earnings per share growth of 25 to 30 percent for next several years. Set a 12-18 month price target in the mid-$50s.

-- For Host Marriott, said set a 12-18 month price target in the low-to-mid $20s. Said expects Host Marriott's portfolio of upscale, full-service hotels to continue to produce impressive revenue and EBITDA growth for at least the next two years.
-- On Bristol Hotels, said expects shares to trade in low-$30s within the next 12-18 months.
-- said started Promus Hotels as a hold since the stock has performed very strongly so far in 1997 and is approaching the low-to-mid-40s price target.

-- Said started ITT as a buy, but cautioned that it has concerns about the company's longer-term prospects if ITT were to successfully defend itself against Hilton Hotels Corp's hostile bid and remain independent. Said the near-term performance of ITT's stock will move as a function of how the fight for the company unfolds. Said believes ITT will remain independent. Said to achieve that goal, is expected to propose a self-tender for at least $70 a share.
